provenance.note: Winner profile selected by the r66 select-transfer decision (factor B, reduction 1.0) with the registered factor-D receive buffer (25 MiB, reduction 1.0 in the r66 matrix) applied per the user's G003 directive after r71 located the default-buffer kernel-cleanliness boundary between 5k and 10k. Constants only, no measurement claims. ackReflector native added 2026-09-02 under the S4 native-path amendment: acks are reflected in the native crate, never through the shard's JS loop. serverWorkers 3 added 2026-09-02 for the r86 worker-count A/B (lever 3): same ladder, 3 Tokio workers per shard on 24 shards; the 2-worker baseline is r85. serverGro off added 2026-09-02 for the r92 GRO mis-steering A/B; r91 (gro on, default) is the baseline. serverWorkers back to 2 on 2026-09-03 for the r96 40k A/B: r95 (GRO off, 3 workers) made 30k CLEAN and 40k lossless-but-unclean (ack p99 137 ms, 9.5 MB shard socket backlog at 84% box CPU); r96 tests runtime oversubscription with the same GRO-off profile. r97 (2026-09-03, "cheaper receiver"): serverGro back on, serverWorkers 3, endpoints 40000 = one generator source port per session (ports 20000-59999) so kernel GRO can never merge datagrams of different QUIC connections while the server keeps GRO receive savings; r95 (GRO off, 128 endpoints) is the lossless baseline, r96 showed 2 workers regress 30k. r98 (2026-09-03): back to endpoints 128 and serverGro off (r95 lossless baseline); serverWorkers 4 to test whether the r95 40k ack tail (137 ms, starved endpoint reader, per-worker util 0.58) is Tokio-worker scheduling; r96 showed 2 workers regress 30k. The r97 endpoints-40000 arm was retired pre-launch (2.9 MiB per quinn endpoint). Restored serverWorkers 3 after r98: 2 (r96) and 4 (r98) both regress the 30k ack tail; 3 is the measured optimum on c-48-intel with 24 shards. serverRecvRuntime dedicated added 2026-09-03 for the r99 A/B: quinn's endpoint driver on its own thread per shard; r95 (shared, 3 workers, GRO off) is the baseline whose 40k rung was lossless but 137 ms p99 with a 9.5 MB socket backlog. r100 (2026-09-03): serverRecvRuntime back to shared (r99 dedicated reader regressed 30k to 214 ms); ackCadence relaxed = server max_ack_delay 100 ms + ACK_FREQUENCY to the client (threshold 10, 100 ms) to cut the ~30% ACK-only packets on both directions (r95 40k: 1.304 packets/frame, 41 cores). r102 (2026-09-04): ackCadence back to default (r101 relaxed failed 20k twice with one-session connect errors, not root-caused) and pacerPps 30000 = the paced-mirror emitter at 30,000 datagrams/s per shard (40k over 24 shards is ~25,000/s per shard plus headroom) to test whether the r95 40k ack tail is the connection drivers queueing behind each 20 ms fan-out burst on the shared Tokio pool; r95 (unpaced, pacerPps 0) is the baseline. r102 refuted pacing (30k ack p99 594 ms vs r95 9 ms, +4.5 cores, identical packet counts; 20k 2/2 clean with cadence default). r103 (2026-09-04): pacerPps back to 0 and ackCadence relaxed again, unchanged otherwise, to reproduce r101's one-session 20k connect failures with the shard now writing native warn/error events (the handshake-failure chain carrying any H3 close) to stderr, persisted per shard in the diagnostic. r103 refuted relaxed cadence (30k ack p99 523 ms vs 9 ms at the same CPU; 20k clean 2/2, r101 not reproduced). r104 (2026-09-04): ackCadence back to default, pacerPps 0, udpSendBatch 64 = the addon's cross-connection sendmmsg batching (up to 64 datagrams per syscall from one flusher thread per shard) on the r95 profile, to test whether the r95 40k ack tail is the per-transmit sendmsg cost on the shared Tokio pool; r95 (udpSendBatch 0) is the baseline.
